newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate debt firm amid supply, Marvel mired.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate debt firm amid supply, Marvel mired.

text.p: U.S. corporate investors took in another $1.0 billion in supply on Thursday and dealers continued pricing deals through the market, while Marvel Entertainment was again tossed about in the junk bond arena, dealers across both markets said.

Meanwhile, Westinghouse Electric Corp. debt tightened 10 to 15 basis points after the company announced on Wednesday that it will spin off its industrials businesses. The move was widely expected and welcomed by the market.
"The market has given its vote of confidence to the idea of lumping the debt with broadcasting assets," a trader said.
Back in the high-grade market, secondary and new issue spreads were said to be firm despite spots of widening for some fresh paper.

TransAmerica Corp's $200 million A2/single-A rated 10-year notes, priced on Wednesday as 6-3/4s to yield 60 basis points over the Treasury curve, were bid at 63 basis points near the close, one trader said.
Tuesday's $200 million Commercial Credit 10-year notes widened to a 52 basis point bid from 47.5.
High-grade issuance on Wednesday also included:

--$450 million Ba1/BBB-minus rated two-part debt from Freeport-McMoran Copper & Gold via UBS Securities. A $200 million tranche of 10-year debt was priced as 7-1/2s to yield 135 basis points over Treasuries and another $250 million 30-year debt, putable in seven years, was priced as 7.20s to yield 110 basis over.
--$150 million A3/A-minus rated 10-year senior notes from Enron Oil & Gas priced as 6.70s to yield 50 basis points over.
--Finally, $200 million A2/A-minus rated 6-5/8 percent seven-year notes from Smith Barney Holdings Inc priced to yield 60 basis points over Treasuries.
Turning to high-yielders, Marvel Holdings Inc and Marvel (Parent) Holdings' zero coupon bonds regained composure after Tuesday's bloodbath but still slipped another point or two.
At the close, the old bonds were quoted at 17 bid, 18 offer and the new bonds were quoted at 14-1/2 bid, 16 offer.

Marvel shares and debt sank on Tuesday after Andrews Group Inc offered to buy 80.1 percent of new Marvel common stock for $350 million, well below market cost. The acquisition would be paid for in cash and/or Toy Biz Inc common stock.
The deal would dilute current shares which back the outstanding Marvel stock-secured debt.

Phelps Hoyt, vice president of KDP Investment Advisors Inc, issued a buy recommendation on Marvel based on his belief that a better offer from controlling shareholder Ronald Perelman was likely. Hoyt added the debt would be better valued under bankruptcy than Perelman's current plan.
Other high-yield trade was quiet although prices managed 1/8 to 1/4 point gains on average, traders said.
Telecom paper continued to garner much of that interest and outperformed the pack, as evidenced by Sprint Spectrum zero's 3/4 point gain. British names were also active.
But troubled MobilMedia zeros of 2003 quietly faded another three points to 45 bid, a trader said.
New issues were again the belle of the market.

--Cole National Corp's $150 million 144a 10-year senior subordinated notes, priced as 9-7/8s to yield 9.991 percent or 379 basis points over Treasuries, was quoted at 100-1/8 bid, 100-1/2 offer at the close.
--Blue Bird Body Co's $100 million 144a 10-year senior subordinated notes, priced as 10-3/4s to yield 10.80 or 460 basis points over, went out with a 102 bid.
The 30-year T-bond closed down 1/8 to yield 6.45 percent.
